class.name: Sky
class.brief_description: Defines a 3D environment's background by using a [Material].
class.description: The [Sky] class uses a [Material] to render a 3D environment's background and the light it emits by updating the reflection/radiance cubemaps.

method.name: get_layer_generations
method.description: Debug only. Returns the generation ID of each roughness layer of the published radiance map, so you can see which layers came from which update. See [method RenderingServer.sky_debug_get_layer_generations] for the meaning of the values.

method.name: get_radiance_generation
method.description: Returns the generation ID of the published radiance map. The ID goes up by one with every published update and never goes back down. [code]0[/code] means that no radiance map has been published yet. Compare two values to tell whether the lighting from this [Sky] has changed.

method.name: get_sh_buffer
method.description: Returns the storage buffer that holds the diffuse spherical harmonics of the [Sky], or an invalid [RID] when they are off (see [member sh_enabled]). The layout is described in [method RenderingServer.sky_get_sh_buffer]. The [RID] changes when the radiance map is created again, so read it again each frame instead of keeping it.

method.name: get_sh_debug
method.description: Debug only. Reads the published spherical harmonics back from the GPU and returns them as a dictionary. This stalls the renderer until the GPU is done, so do not call it in a game loop. See [method RenderingServer.sky_debug_get_sh] for the keys.

method.name: get_update_stats
method.description: Returns the update counters of the [Sky], such as the number of cycles started and completed, the number of publishes and the current generation. See [method RenderingServer.sky_get_update_stats] for the keys. The dictionary is empty when the [Sky] does not exist.

method.name: request_radiance_update
method.description: Starts an update of the radiance map. If an update is already running, the request is kept and starts the next update as soon as the running one is published. This is the only way to start an update while [member radiance_update_policy] is [constant RADIANCE_UPDATE_POLICY_MANUAL]. See [method RenderingServer.sky_request_radiance_update].

members.member: The method for generating the radiance map from the sky. The radiance map is a cubemap with increasingly blurry versions of the sky corresponding to different levels of roughness. Radiance maps can be expensive to calculate.

The [Sky]'s radiance map size. The higher the radiance map size, the more detailed the lighting from the [Sky] will be. [b]Note:[/b] Some hardware will have trouble with higher radiance sizes, especially [constant RADIANCE_SIZE_512] and above. Only use such high values on high-end hardware.

When the radiance map is updated. With [constant RADIANCE_UPDATE_POLICY_AUTOMATIC] (the default) the engine starts an update on its own when the sky material, lights, fog, time or camera position change. With [constant RADIANCE_UPDATE_POLICY_MANUAL] only [method request_radiance_update] starts an update. A missing radiance map, a change of [member radiance_size] and a change of [member process_mode] still update it. The visible sky is drawn every frame in both policies.

If [code]true[/code], the diffuse spherical harmonics of the [Sky] are computed every time a radiance update is published, and they carry the same generation ID as the radiance map. Read them with [method get_sh_buffer]. They are off by default and cost nothing while off. See [method RenderingServer.sky_set_sh_enabled].
[Material] used to draw the background. Can be [PanoramaSkyMaterial], [ProceduralSkyMaterial], [PhysicalSkyMaterial], or even a [ShaderMaterial] if you want to use your own custom shader.

constants.constant: Represents the size of the [enum RadianceSize] enum.

Automatically selects the appropriate process mode based on your sky shader. If your shader uses [code]TIME[/code] or [code]POSITION[/code], this will use [constant PROCESS_MODE_REALTIME]. If your shader uses any of the [code]LIGHT_*[/code] variables or any custom uniforms, this uses [constant PROCESS_MODE_INCREMENTAL]. Otherwise, this defaults to [constant PROCESS_MODE_QUALITY].

Uses high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map. In general, this results in much higher quality than [constant PROCESS_MODE_REALTIME] but takes much longer to generate. This should not be used if you plan on changing the sky at runtime. If you are finding that the reflection is not blurry enough and is showing sparkles or fireflies, try increasing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/ggx_samples].

Uses the same high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map as [constant PROCESS_MODE_QUALITY], but updates over several frames. The number of frames is determined by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers]. Use this when you need highest quality radiance maps, but have a sky that updates slowly.

Uses the fast filtering algorithm to process the radiance map. In general this results in lower quality, but substantially faster run times. If you need better quality, but still need to update the sky every frame, consider turning on [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/fast_filter_high_quality]. [b]Note:[/b] The fast filtering algorithm is limited to 256×256 cubemaps, so [member radiance_size] must be set to [constant RADIANCE_SIZE_256]. Otherwise, a warning is printed and the overridden radiance size is ignored.
The engine decides when the radiance map is updated, from its own checks on the sky material, lights, fog, time and camera position. This is the default.

The radiance map is updated only when [method request_radiance_update] is called. Changes of the sky material, lights and fog do not update it on their own. Use this when the sky is expensive to filter and the game knows when it has changed enough to need a new map.
